audit.answered: answered a question of {agent} on task {task}
audit.canceled: canceled a question of {agent} on task {task}

errors.continuation_run: this run is answering a chat message: ask in your reply instead of with task_ask
errors.not_running: only the run working on the task may ask, and the task is {status}
errors.own_task_only: an agent run asks only on its own task
errors.stage_run_only: only an agent's stage run may ask questions: a chat, the auditor or a person comments instead

prompts.brief_how_to_ask:
## Asking a person

When you cannot go on without something only a person can decide or give you (a choice the task leaves open, a credential or an access you lack, a contradiction in the request), ask with `task_ask` instead of guessing. Do not ask what the description, the comments or the repository already answer.

- Ask once, with everything you need: up to 4 questions per call, each with up to 6 short options when the choices are clear. Put what you found in `context`.
- A blocking question: call `task_ask` and end your turn. Do not keep working on what depends on the answer. The answers come back to you in this same conversation.
- A question that does not block carries a `default`: say what you will do if nobody answers, then keep working on it. An answer may reach you while you work.
- `blocker` is for what you cannot do at all without the person (a key, an access). Pick it only then.

A run may ask {per_run} times at most, and a task may have {open} questions open.
prompts.brief_open_heading:
## Open questions

Asked and still unanswered. Do not ask them again.
prompts.instruction_blocking: Your question is posted. End your turn now and do not keep working on what depends on the answer: when a person answers, you are resumed in this same conversation with the answers.
prompts.instruction_non_blocking: Your question is posted. Keep working with your default ({default}). If an answer arrives while you work it reaches you here; otherwise it stays in the task's thread.
